newsitem.title: USA: Four killed in Everglades chopper crash.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in Everglades chopper crash.

text.p: A helicopter spraying pesticides over the Florida Everglades crashed on Thursday, killing the pilot and three other people on board, a rescue official said.
"It appears it hit some kind of radio mast. The wreckage is lying about 200 yards from the tower," said Gene Herrera, spokesman for the Broward County Fire and Rescue Department.
The helicopter went down about a mile (1.6 kms) north of Interstate 75 and U.S. 27, known as Alligator Alley. The wreckage fell on the edge of a parking lot used by campers and fishermen.
"We have four confirmed fatalities," Herrera said.
The helicopter was believed to have been contracted by the South Florida Water Management to spray pesticides over the Everglades.
Rescue teams could not recover the bodies until they had ascertained what pesticides the helicopter was carrying in case there was a risk of explosion, Herrera added.
